answers.answer: Separate Conflict cards by backs I/II/III; shuffle all four III and place them face down, shuffle II and deal five face down on top, then shuffle I and deal one face down on top, making a 10-card deck. Return unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘1 Conflict I on top, 5 Conflict II below it, 4 Conflict III on the bottom’; ‘Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.’

answers.answer: In four-player human setup, start at 1 VP; in a three-player game, start at 0 VP. Each gets two Agents on the Leader plus the third Swordmaster beside the board, three troops in the nearby garrison and nine in supply, and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘on the 1 space in a 4-player game, otherwise on the 0 space’; ‘Place two Agents on your Leader and your third Agent (your Swordmaster) next to the game board’; ‘three’ troops in garrison and ‘remaining nine’ in supply; ‘Take 1 water.’

answers.answer: Yes, you may Reveal while Agents remain; after taking a Reveal turn you skip the rest of Player Turns, so you cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed in the Reveal step, not Agent-turn cards. Clean Up moves all cards in front of you, from Agent and Reveal turns, to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘Agent turns are optional; you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents’; ‘Once you've taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped’; ‘Reveal box effects of the just-revealed cards only’; ‘Move all cards in front of you … to your discard pile.’

answers.answer: Resources granted by a Plot Intrigue played before placing your Agent can pay that destination’s entry cost. Resources gained only after placement, from the destination or played Agent card, cannot pay that same entry. One card chooses only one Agent icon and cannot send multiple Agents; a card without Agent icons can only be revealed, not played on an Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot may be played before placing; ‘resources it grants before entry join your available supply’; post-placement gains ‘cannot pay for that same entry’; ‘one card can't send multiple Agents’; no-icon cards ‘may only be revealed’.

answers.answer: You may deploy the three troops recruited this turn plus up to two of the four already in your garrison, for a maximum of five. At a non-Combat destination you do not deploy units. Recruited troops come from your supply and are placed in your garrison until deployment.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: ‘any or all units recruited during your current turn … plus up to two more units from your garrison’; only ‘Combat space’; the cube icon takes a troop ‘from your supply and place[s] it in your garrison.’

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon on a card lets you send an Agent to a space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; it does not recall that Spy. Infiltrate lets you recall your Spy from a post connected to an opponent-occupied destination to ignore that opponent’s Agent and use that space. Gather Intelligence lets you recall a Spy connected to the space you visit to draw a card. The same Spy cannot pay for both effects, though different Spies can be used for one of each. Choose Gather Intelligence just after placing the Agent and before any space or card effects.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spy Agent icon allows connected access and ‘you do not recall the Spy’; Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence definitions; cannot recall the same Spy for both; Gather timing is ‘immediately after placing your Agent (before receiving any effects…)’.

answers.answer: Strength is 2 per troop, 3 per sandworm and 1 per revealed sword: 2 troops + 1 sandworm + 4 swords = 11. If your final unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. You need at least one unit in the Conflict to play Combat Intrigue.
answers.evidence: Strength: ‘Each troop … 2’; ‘each sandworm … 3’; ‘each sword … 1’; ‘if your last unit is ever removed, your strength becomes 0.’ Combat Intrigue begins with players with ‘at least one unit in the Conflict’.

answers.answer: Yes; a player may act again after previously passing if another player then plays a Combat Intrigue. The window closes when all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison), sandworms return to the bank, and Combat markers reset to 0.
answers.evidence: Combat: ‘not required to pass just because you passed earlier’; resolve once ‘all players involved in Combat pass consecutively’; cleanup returns troops to supply, sandworms to bank, markers reset.

answers.answer: If two tie for first, each takes the second reward, neither wins the Conflict and neither takes the Conflict card, in both four- and three-player play. In four players, the remaining players may compete for third if exactly two tied for first; in three or fewer players no other rewards are given. A 0-strength player receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tied first each gain second; ‘no one wins the Conflict or takes the Conflict card’; four-player exactly two tie permits remaining players to compete for third; ‘A player with 0 strength receives no reward.’

answers.answer: Having one or more sandworms doubles rewards once; two worms do not quadruple rewards. Control of a location and battle icons on Conflict cards cannot be doubled. If a reward lets you pay 3 spice for 1 VP, doubling permits paying the cost a second time: pay 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 spice for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: ‘one or more sandworms … double’; control and battle icons cannot; optional cost may be paid a second time; example: 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 for 2.

answers.answer: Check a normal battle-icon match when you win a Conflict and take its card into your supply; a matching face-up Conflict or Objective card qualifies. Matching is mandatory when a match exists: flip the pair face down and gain 1 VP. During Endgame the wild icon can match any one of the three icon types in your supply; flip the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: upon winning/taking the card, check another ‘face-up Conflict or Objective card’; ‘must flip’ a matching pair for 1 VP; during Endgame wild may match any one of the three icons.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; that VP is lost below 2 and regained on returning to 2. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained below 4 and earned again on returning to 4; the first player to 4 also gets the Alliance and 1 VP, which stays tied to holding that token. Merely tying the holder at 4 does not take it; an opponent must rise higher (subject to the stated FAQ holder-loss rules).
answers.evidence: Scoring: 2 Influence VP reverses below 2; 4 Influence has separate track bonus retained below 4 and Alliance +1 VP; ‘Tying the current holder does not steal the Alliance: an opponent must rise higher.’

answers.answer: During Reveal, spend Persuasion before, between or after Reveal effects. You may pool sources to buy one card and split a source across cards. The Imperium Row is replenished to five, so after buying you may buy its replacement if affordable. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: may use Persuasion ‘before, between, or after’ effects; pool or split; row always five and replacement may be acquired; acquired card ‘goes face up into your discard pile’.

answers.answer: At a Maker space, gain all accumulated bonus spice there even when choosing the sandworm option; a space without an Agent receives 1 more spice in its bonus spot during Makers. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two worms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one worm. Hooks are not spent. While the Shield Wall remains, worms cannot be summoned to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery or Imperial Basin; once removed they can go to any Conflict. Worms can never go in a garrison and return to the bank after Combat.
answers.evidence: Actions/Sandworms and Board Space Guide: ‘gain all the bonus spice’; Deep Desert/Hagga costs and choices; Hooks ‘never spent’; Shield Wall protects named three locations; ‘A sandworm can never be placed in a garrison.’

answers.answer: At the end of a round, 10 or more VP by any player or an empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigue, then compare VP; the most VP wins. Rulebook tie-breakers are spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory Conditions: ‘At the end of a round’; Endgame Intrigue first, then most VP; tiebreakers ‘amount of spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.’

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM starts with two contracts face up and 18 face down from the 20 standard contracts. Add four Intrigue cards to that deck and four Imperium cards to that deck. Shaddam Corrino IV is an optional Leader, not compulsory. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts stay in the box and are not part of this setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup: shuffle 20, flip two and leave 18 in bank; add 4 cards to each deck; Shaddam is an option; contrasting-back 10 are separate Rise of Ix set, leave in box.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon takes one of the two face-up contracts and replaces it with a face-up contract from the bank; without CHOAM, or when all contracts are taken, it gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract completes by visiting a Maker space and gaining its shown spice amount that turn in total; Immediate completes as soon as taken; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes the next time you acquire that card.
answers.evidence: CHOAM: contract icon behavior and fallback; contract completion definitions for Harvest, Immediate and Acquire The Spice Must Flow.

answers.answer: No. If you take a contract for a space after already sending your Agent there this turn, wait until a future turn; you must hold the contract when sending the Agent. When complete, announce it, gain its shown rewards, flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: CHOAM: ‘must wait until a future turn’; ‘must have had the contract at the time you sent your Agent’; on completion ‘announce it, gain the rewards … flip it face down and leave it in your supply.’

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. The Rival gets Ornithopter Objective; two eligible Objectives are dealt to humans, and the First Player marker goes to the human whose Objective shows it. Turn order is First Player → Rival → other human; First Player alternates between the humans only. The Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival: ‘one shared scoring Rival’; ‘Give the Rival the Ornithopter Objective’; First Player human from other cards; order First Player → Rival → other human; Rival ‘never Reveals.’

answers.answer: For an occupied destination, ignore it and reveal another Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: attempt an empty post of the specified type; if none, ignore the placement; either way reveal another Hagal card and continue the turn. Ignore ordinary space costs and effects, applying only Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: ignore occupied destination and reveal again; Place Spy behavior; ‘Ignore normal space costs and effects’; if deck empties or Reshuffle, reshuffle immediately and continue.

answers.answer: In three- or four-player setup, shuffle Objectives after removing those marked for a different player count; each player draws one at random. First Player is whoever drew the card showing the First Player marker. Shaddam may be selected only when using the CHOAM Module.
answers.evidence: Setup: omit mismatched 1-3P/4/6P cards, each draws one at random, Objective showing First Player marker determines it; Shaddam ‘Do not use … unless playing with the CHOAM Module.’

answers.answer: The bank’s Solari, spice, water and sandworms are not limited; make a convenient substitution if depleted. By contrast, if your personal troop supply is empty, you cannot recruit more until troops return there. Pay resource costs to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup: resources and sandworms ‘not meant to be limited — make any convenient substitution’; if no troops in supply, cannot recruit until some return; payments return to bank.

answers.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal and place the new Conflict, resolve any defensive troop bonus, then each player draws five cards. If Endgame is not triggered at Recall, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player marker clockwise and begin the next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure lists five phases; Phase 1 reveals Conflict and defensive bonus before each draws five; Phase 5 next-round procedure.

answers.answer: Yes, board-space and Agent-box effects can be taken in any order, and on a Faction space you also advance Influence; the effects may be carried out in any order. No, entry costs and requirements must be met before effects, so Influence gained by that visit cannot meet its own entry requirement.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs/meet requirements first; ‘Then gain’ space and Agent effects, and Influence; ‘You may carry out all these effects in any order.’

answers.answer: An optional arrow cost can normally be paid only once per turn, so you cannot repeat it for a second effect; sandworm reward doubling is the exception for a Conflict-card reward. Most card and space effects are mandatory; ‘may,’ optional arrow costs, and the black-X trash icon are exceptions. Intrigue conditions and costs must be met to play it.
answers.evidence: Arrows: cost/effect only once per turn except doubled Conflict rewards; FAQ: most effects mandatory with listed exceptions; Intrigue conditions and costs must be met.

answers.answer: Place a Spy from your supply on an unoccupied observation post. If none is in supply, you may first recall one of your deployed Spies for no effect. If the placement effect specifies an Agent-icon type, only a post connected to that icon qualifies.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spy icon places on unoccupied post; if no Spies in supply, may recall one for no effect; specified icon must connect to post.

answers.answer: Infiltrate is described for sending to a board space occupied by another player; using it to bypass your own occupied space is unsupported. A Spy cannot send an Agent without playing a card for the Agent turn. You cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement; you may use one for Infiltrate and another for Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Special Rules defines Infiltrate only for another player’s Agent; FAQ says recalling Spy ‘still requires playing a card for the Agent turn’ and permits one Infiltrate plus one Gather, ‘never two to Gather Intelligence.’ Own-occupancy case not stated.

answers.answer: The controller gets the separate control bonus whenever any player, including the controller, visits: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin. A Conflict winner takes control by placing a marker and replacing an opponent’s marker. The defensive troop comes from the controller’s supply and may be deployed when that location’s Conflict is revealed, with no Agent visit.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: controller receives bonus whenever ‘any player (yourself included)’ visits; winner replaces marker; upon reveal controller may deploy one troop from supply ‘without an Agent visit.’

answers.answer: In a three-player tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; the Conflict winner keeps rewards/card and no further rewards are given. Players tied for third receive nothing. If three players tie for first, each gets second reward and no one wins or takes the card; in four players a tie of three or more for first yields no other rewards.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tie for second gets third reward; tie for third gets nothing; tie first conditions for 3-or-fewer and 4-player games.

answers.answer: In an ordinary three-player Conflict with three distinct positive strengths, first and second receive their rewards, and third receives nothing. A Rival counts as a player in the standard two-player game; ordinary first and second get rewards and third gets nothing unless tie-for-second rules apply.
answers.evidence: Combat: with 2 or 3 players, ordinary first and second receive rewards, third none; printed third only for tie second; explicitly includes two humans plus Rival.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigue can be played on your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigue only during Combat; Endgame Intrigue only at game end. Keep Intrigues face down, separate from your deck, and reveal only when played; after resolving, put them face up in a discard pile next to the Intrigue Deck. If the Intrigue Deck runs out, shuffle its discard into a new deck.
answers.evidence: Special Rules Intrigue card types and storage/discard; FAQ: if Intrigue deck runs out, shuffle its discard to form a new deck.

answers.answer: An ordinary discard instruction discards a card of your choice from your hand, not an Intrigue unless specified. Secrets’ Steal Intrigue effect takes one card selected at random from each opponent who has four or more Intrigue cards.
answers.evidence: Discarding: from hand and cannot be Intrigue unless specified; Intrigue cards: each opponent with four or more gives one selected at random.

answers.answer: Trash effects may remove cards from hand, discard pile or in play. Ordinary trashed cards go to the box; Reserve cards go back to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or the card says to trash itself. Trashing The Spice Must Flow does not remove its acquired VP; that VP is retained.
answers.evidence: Trashing section and Victory FAQ: ‘The Spice Must Flow’s acquire VP is retained if the card is later trashed.’

answers.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once at the moment you acquire the card. When unable to draw because your deck is empty, reshuffle the discard pile into a new deck and continue drawing. Unused Persuasion is lost at the end of Reveal and cannot be carried over.
answers.evidence: Acquire box: effect ‘at the moment you acquire’; Acquiring Cards: reshuffle discard when deck empty; Persuasion ‘can never be saved.’

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and revealed in the Reveal turn are in play until Clean Up, unless trashed first. Two Fremen Bond cards can activate one another regardless of order played, as each checks for another Fremen card in play. Clean Up ends their in-play state by moving them to discard.
answers.evidence: In play/Fremen Bond: played and revealed cards remain face up/in play until Clean Up; Bond cards activate one another regardless of order.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the one just placed; the recalled Agent can be used again on another Agent turn in the same round. Retreat moves a troop from Conflict to garrison. ‘Retreat any number’ can mean zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon and Retreat definitions; FAQ: ‘Retreat any number’ allows zero.

answers.answer: A single free-choice effect granting two Influence cannot split it across Factions; choose one Faction for both. An Alliance-icon effect requires holding that Faction’s Alliance token. A minimum-Influence effect requires that threshold with its named Faction.
answers.evidence: Special Rules Influence: freely chosen gain two ‘can't choose two different Factions’; Alliance icon requires token; some effects require minimum Influence.

answers.answer: If the Alliance holder loses Influence while tied with two opponents, the former holder chooses which tied player receives the token. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4 or more to take it, return the token to the board; the holder loses its VP.
answers.evidence: FAQ Alliance loss: if several tied, former holder chooses; falling to 3 or lower loses Alliance, return to board if nobody has 4+, and losing it loses VP.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used this turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, in addition to the next five-card draw. A Plot Intrigue with a later Reveal effect remains face up until that effect resolves, then is discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ Draw timing: during Reveal immediately reveal/use; after Reveal keep for next round and draw five more; Plot with later Reveal stays face up, is used, then discarded.

answers.answer: No, a ‘when you win’ Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first because no one wins the Conflict. If received as a reward for an outright win, it may be played immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ Combat: ‘When you win a Conflict’ Intrigues cannot be played after tying for first; if received as winning reward they can be played immediately.

answers.answer: If final VP and all four resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed 12-space track.
answers.evidence: Victory FAQ: if all four resource tiebreakers tied, most recent Reveal-turn player wins; ‘Scores may exceed the printed track’s 12.’

answers.answer: No. Complete all contracts held for the same space with one Agent placement; they cannot be delayed until later after visiting. Contract completion is another effect of that Agent turn and can resolve in any order with space and Agent-box effects, but the contract must have been held when the Agent was sent.
answers.evidence: FAQ Contract completion: fulfill all held same-space contracts with one placement; completion is another effect and may resolve in any order; must hold it when sending Agent.

answers.answer: Shaddam does not start with set-aside Sardaukar contracts; they do not start in his possession. With Sardaukar Commander, when acquiring a contract he may choose one set-aside Sardaukar contract instead of a generally available contract. His Emperor of the Known Universe deployment restriction starts immediately when playing Signet Ring to send an Agent and lasts for that turn, not the round.
answers.evidence: FAQ Shaddam: set-aside contracts do not start in possession; Sardaukar Commander allows choice on acquiring; restriction immediate on Signet Ring, ‘lasts only for that turn, not the round.’

answers.answer: Feyd’s token starts at the leftmost space of his Training track and stays at the rightmost space after reaching it. Lady Jessica begins with her Lady Jessica side face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications state all three details.

answers.answer: Moving from 1 to 3 reaches 2, even when moving past 2 while gaining multiple Influence. Margot/Irulan can reach 2 with the same Faction more than once after losing and later regaining Influence; moving down through 2 does not count. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild’s Favor from play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications on reaching 2, repeat reach and descending; Spacing Guild’s Favor only triggers when discarded from hand.

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses the Spice Trade icon; without CHOAM it gives 2 Solari, and with CHOAM it takes/replaces a contract (reverting to 2 Solari if none remain); it also draws a card. Dutiful Service uses Emperor, gives 1 Emperor Influence, then takes/replaces a contract with CHOAM or gives 2 Solari without/if none remain. Accept Contract gives no automatic Faction Influence; Dutiful Service’s explicitly listed Emperor Influence is its effect.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Accept Contract (Spice Trade), card draw and contract/2 Solari; Dutiful Service (Emperor), 1 Emperor Influence and contract/2 Solari. Guide says Landsraad, City and Spice Trade are not Factions and Accept Contract gives no automatic Influence.

answers.answer: Arrakeen is City and Combat, costs nothing, and visitor recruits one troop and draws one card (plus controller gets 1 Solari). Fremkit is Fremen and Combat, costs nothing, gives 1 Fremen Influence and draws a card. Research Station is City and Combat, costs 2 water and recruits two troops and draws two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows for Arrakeen, Fremkit and Research Station.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water; choose 4 base spice or, with Hooks, summon two worms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water; choose 2 base spice or, with Hooks, summon one worm. Both choices still collect all accumulated bonus spice. Hooks are not spent to summon; Shield Wall still prohibits protected-location summoning.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows: both gain all bonus spice and list costs/base/worm choice; Sandworms: Hooks retained, Shield Wall restriction.

answers.answer: Sietch Tabr requires 2+ Fremen Influence and is Combat. Choose either: take Maker Hooks if lacking, recruit one troop and gain 1 water; or gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall. The second option gives no troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Sietch Tabr row lists the two choices; only first includes recruiting a troop.

answers.answer: Each High Council visit costs 5 Solari and it is not a Combat space. On the first visit, place your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gain 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. On subsequent visits, gain 2 spice, draw an Intrigue and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide High Council row.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone obtains a Swordmaster and 6 Solari once anyone does; each player may take it only once per game. The new third Agent is available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival taking its Swordmaster also lowers the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Swordmaster row; Rival resources section says Rival gaining Swordmaster reduces human cost to 6.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses Landsraad, requires 2+ Emperor Influence and costs 3 Solari. Its effects let you discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue, and recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically grant Emperor Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Imperial Privilege row; guide notes this is not a Faction space and only explicit listed Influence effects apply.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade, requires 2+ Guild Influence and costs 3 spice. It gains 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; the free-choice Influence need not be Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Shipping row.

answers.answer: Gather Support (Landsraad, not Combat) lets you choose 0 or 2 Solari; recruit two troops, and if you pay 2 Solari also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery (City, Combat) lets you choose 0 or 1 spice; gain 2 Solari, or 4 Solari if you paid 1 spice; controller separately gets 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows for Gather Support and Spice Refinery, including Combat labels.

answers.answer: Heighliner is Spacing Guild/Combat, costs 5 spice, gains 1 Guild Influence and recruits five troops. Desert Tactics is Fremen/Combat, costs 1 water, gains 1 Fremen Influence, recruits one troop and may trash a card. Sardaukar is Emperor and not Combat, costs 4 spice, gains 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue and recruits four troops. Only Heighliner and Desert Tactics allow normal deployment at their Combat spaces.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows give costs, icons, effects and Combat labels.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall uses Landsraad, costs nothing, draws an Intrigue and gives 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn if your Agent is there. Espionage uses Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice, gives 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draws a card and places a Spy. Deliver Supplies uses Spacing Guild, costs nothing and gives 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows for Assembly Hall, Espionage and Deliver Supplies.

answers.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent’s destination that turn; it can be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear’s red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ False Orders and Litany Against Fear clarifications.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If nobody acquires it by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ Manipulate clarification.

answers.answer: The Rival starts with four cubes at the bottoms of Influence tracks, three troops in its garrison and the remaining troops in supply, two Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside the board, three Spies and 1 water; its score and Combat marker are 0. Shuffle House Hagal retaining the 2P Reshuffle card. Its 10+ VP can trigger Endgame at Recall and it can win as a scoring competitor.
answers.evidence: Required Rival setup and opening paragraph: stated starting components, 2P Reshuffle and Rival’s 10+ VP triggers Endgame.

answers.answer: As soon as the Rival’s counted resources reach its printed Swordmaster threshold, it spends that many and takes its third Agent, usable in the current round. Count Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water together, each as one; spend Solari first, then spice, then Intrigue cards, then water, keeping leftovers. The Rival threshold is printed on its card; its numeric value is not supplied in the summary.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster section gives trigger, resource count/order/leftovers and states printed threshold; exact numeric threshold depends on its Rival card and is unsupported here.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, the Rival spends each set of 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards or 3 water for 1 VP. It cannot combine a mixed total of seven resources for a VP; the sets are specific resource types.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources: ‘whenever it has 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water, spend each such set for 1 VP.’

answers.answer: When choosing Influence, the Rival picks the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by leftmost priority. It gets the VP at 2 and Alliance VP like a human, but not the resource track bonus for reaching 4. A numbered Hagal Influence icon refers to that position in the Rival card’s Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat/resource rules: least Influence and leftmost priority; gets Influence VP and Alliances but no 4-Influence resource bonus; numbered icon definition.

answers.answer: It must select one destination according to the current condition and cannot use the other if that selected one is occupied; it reveals a new card. Select Accept Contract/Shipping based on Guild Influence, and Deliver Supplies/Heighliner based on Conflict tier.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: two-destination card selects only the destination matching conditions; if occupied reveal new card without other destination; stated selection conditions.

answers.answer: At a Combat space the Rival may deploy up to two available garrison troops even if that Hagal card recruited none. At a noncombat space, troops recruited from supply go to garrison. A conditional 2+ Influence bonus not met does not prevent Agent placement; apply only the Hagal effects available under the condition.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: Combat space deploy up to two garrison troops even with none recruited; noncombat recruits go in garrison; missing 2+ bonus never prevents placement.

answers.answer: If no post type is specified, choose the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing the third and final supply Spy recalls the Rival’s other two Spies and triggers its Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies to Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes section states each point.

answers.answer: If the Scheme recruits troops before the Rival places an Agent at a Combat space that same turn, deploy those troops too. A Place Spy card with no legal post is ignored, and the Rival immediately reveals another Hagal card and continues that Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes: Scheme recruits before placement count toward deployment; Place Spy no-post rule says reveal another card either way.

answers.answer: At Hagga/Deep Desert the Rival collects all bonus spice. With Hooks and a Conflict that permits worms, it summons one/two respectively instead of base spice; without Hooks or if protected Conflict blocks summoning, it takes the base amount instead (Hagga 2, Deep Desert 4). Imperial Basin always gives 1 base spice. The accumulated bonus spice is collected in all cases.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces paragraph.

answers.answer: At start of Combat, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal one Hagal card in turn order and add its bottom swords to strength; if Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window, so may respond after this strength is determined. A Rival with no deployed unit gets no such bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat paragraph: bonus only if at least one unit, bottom swords, Reshuffle procedure, then human Intrigue window.

answers.answer: Yes, the Rival receives control bonuses, defensive troops, battle-icon VP and normal doubled rewards with worms. It always takes optional Conflict VP if able to pay resources or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward gives it 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat paragraph states all items.

answers.answer: During Reveal effects, total Combat strength, announce it, and set the Combat marker at any point while resolving; update it as needed. Over 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn: strength may be totaled/announced/set at any point while resolving and updated; Strength section gives >20 marking.

answers.answer: A Leader’s Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns, not merely when you reveal the card. Cards of any type can override the usual game rules.
answers.evidence: Setup: Signet Ring icon ability activates when playing Signet Ring on an Agent turn, not merely revealing; Overview: cards of any type can override usual rules.

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for a powerful effect. By itself, this icon is not the Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence action; those are separate recall effects you may take without a card when sending an Agent.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Recall Spy icon returns Spy to supply; separate paragraph defines recall without a card for Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence.

answers.answer: The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. Ordinary discard instructions discard a card of your choice from your hand and exclude Intrigue cards unless specified.
answers.evidence: Trashing: trash-an-Intrigue icon; Discarding: hand and not Intrigue unless specified.

answers.answer: Yes. A sandworm doubles a reward granting one Influence of your choice by letting you take the reward a second time; the two instances may choose the same or different Factions. A single effect granting two Influence with free choice must place both with one Faction.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling example: doubled 2 Influence may be with same Faction or two different; Special Rules says single gain-two free choice cannot choose two different.

answers.answer: The Hagal Signet Ring effect resolves its printed Rival Signet Ring ability. The summary says follow the Rival card’s printed Signet Ring and Scheme abilities; a human Signet Ring card or Rival Reveal turn is not required because the Rival never Reveals and follows Hagal effects. The specific effect’s text is not reproduced here.
answers.evidence: Required Rival opening: follow printed Signet Ring and Scheme abilities; Rival never Reveals; Agent turns apply printed Hagal effects. Exact card ability text is not in summary.

answers.answer: A Hagal Maker Hooks icon takes a token only if the Rival needs one; if it already has Hooks it does nothing. A Shield Wall removal effect works only if the Rival has Maker Hooks; without them it is ignored. If the Wall is already gone, there is no token to remove; further behavior is not stated.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces: Hooks icon takes token if needed; Shield Wall effect removes wall only if Rival has Hooks, otherwise ignore. Already-removed case not stated explicitly.

answers.answer: Secrets uses Bene Gesserit, costs nothing, is not Combat, gives 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draws an Intrigue. In addition, each opponent with four or more Intrigues gives one selected at random; these stolen cards come from opponents, while the draw comes from the Intrigue Deck.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Secrets row and Special Rules Steal Intrigue definition.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade, has no entry cost and is Combat. The visitor gains 1 base spice plus all bonus spice there. If that same visitor controls it, the controller separately gains 1 spice too, for an additional control bonus.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Imperial Basin row; guide says resolve visitor and controller effects separately even if same player.

answers.answer: At Round Start, reveal the new Conflict and place it face up next to the deck on top of any Conflict cards left from previous rounds. The summary does not say that unclaimed cards are removed; they remain beneath the new card. Each player draws five only after revealing the Conflict and resolving any defensive troop bonus.
answers.evidence: Phase 1: place new card ‘on top of any Conflict cards remaining from previous rounds’; ‘Then each player draws five cards’ after defensive bonus.

answers.answer: Each human places one cube on the bottom space of each of the four Faction Influence tracks; all four Alliance tokens begin on their marked areas on the tracks, so no one starts holding an Alliance. The Shield Wall token is placed on its marked area below Spice Refinery at setup.
answers.evidence: Setup: Alliance tokens placed on track marked areas; one cube bottom space of each track; Shield Wall placed below Spice Refinery.

answers.answer: In normal three/four-player play, First Player takes the first turn, then turns proceed clockwise, one Agent or Reveal turn at a time. A human who Reveals skips later turns; Player Turns end when all players have Revealed. Combat Intrigue priority starts with First Player and proceeds clockwise; an eligible player may play any number, or pass. The window closes after all players involved pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Player Turns and Combat sections state order, end condition, first player priority, any number, consecutive pass closure.

answers.answer: The three Reveal steps are Reveal Cards, Resolve Reveal Effects, then Clean Up. Effects of revealed cards may be resolved in any order; they do not have to follow card order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn gives ordered three steps and says effects may be resolved ‘in any order.’

answers.answer: Each human shuffles the listed 10-card starting deck and places it face down. Shuffle Intrigue and Imperium decks; deal five Imperium cards face up as the Row; set out Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow Reserve stacks. Without CHOAM, omit CHOAM-marked cards. Each human Combat marker starts at 0; three Spies, Councilor and Control markers are placed in supply, with Control markers and Councilor in view. The specific initial board placement of all three Spies/Councilor/control markers beyond supply/in-view is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Setup gives deck composition/shuffle and Imperium row/reserves/CHOAM omission; Combat marker at 0; ‘remaining components (including your 3 Spies) in your supply, in clear view’; exact individual component placements not otherwise given.

answers.answer: During a Reveal turn, ordinary Persuasion can acquire any of the five Imperium Row cards, Prepare the Way or The Spice Must Flow. Each card’s acquisition cost is at its top right. Ordinary Persuasion purchases are made during Reveal, using Persuasion gained that turn.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: cards and costs, top-right costs; Reveal turn and Persuasion spending.

answers.answer: Ordinary human Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional even when legal. Shield Wall detonation is described as a ‘may remove’ action, so it is optional; once removed, the token returns to the box and cannot return in a later round according to the summary’s described rules.
answers.evidence: Special Rules says ordinary placement and recall optional; Shield Wall ‘may remove the token … (return it to the box)’ and once removed worms may go to any Conflict.

answers.answer: Normally the Agent icon on the played card must match the destination’s icon. A Spy connected to Shipping does not let a card with only City access Shipping. If the played card has a Spy Agent icon, that icon lets you use any space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy, without recalling the Spy.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn matching requirement; clarifying text: connected Spy alone does not give access; Spy Agent icon with Spy at connected post permits access.

answers.answer: Yes. You may play a legal Plot Intrigue before placing the Agent; resources it grants before entry can pay the cost. Resources from the Agent card or destination gained only after placement cannot pay that same entry cost.
answers.evidence: Player Turns specifies Plot before placement and entry resources; post-placement card/space gains cannot pay that entry.

answers.answer: No. In two-player play, skip humans who have Revealed but keep taking the Rival’s Agent turns while it has Agents in supply. Combat begins only after both humans have Revealed and the Rival has used all its Agents. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Phase 2 two-player exception and Rival rules: continue Rival Agents; Combat only after all; Rival never Reveals.

answers.answer: Standard 2–4-player board access/combat reference: Accept Contract—Spice Trade, no; Arrakeen—City, yes; Assembly Hall—Landsraad, no; Deep Desert—Spice Trade, yes; Deliver Supplies—Spacing Guild, no; Desert Tactics—Fremen, yes; Dutiful Service—Emperor, no; Espionage—Bene Gesserit, no; Fremkit—Fremen, yes; Gather Support—Landsraad, no; Hagga Basin—Spice Trade, yes; Heighliner—Spacing Guild, yes; High Council—Landsraad, no; Imperial Basin—Spice Trade, yes; Imperial Privilege—Landsraad, no; Research Station—City, yes; Sardaukar—Emperor, no; Secrets—Bene Gesserit, no; Shipping—Spice Trade, no; Sietch Tabr—City, yes; Spice Refinery—City, yes; Swordmaster—Landsraad, no.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table lists all 22 spaces with Agent icon and marks Combat spaces with label; introductory notes explain icon and Combat notation.

answers.answer: When a Conflict is revealed for a location already under your control, you may deploy one troop from your supply directly to the Conflict; it requires no Agent visit. After rewards, each player returns troops to supply, sandworms return to bank, and all Combat markers reset to 0 before Makers.
answers.evidence: Round Start defensive bonus; Combat cleanup: troop/sandworm return and ‘all Combat markers reset to 0.’

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you and send one Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied matching board space. Resolve that card’s Agent box only; the played card stays in front of you until Clean Up. You cannot reuse a card already in play or discard, nor move an Agent already on the board instead of sending an available Agent from your Leader.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: play one card from hand face up, send Agent from Leader to unoccupied matching space, use Agent box. Setup/turn rules establish Agents from Leader and cards from hand.

answers.answer: The restriction applies immediately when Shaddam plays Signet Ring to send the Agent; he cannot delay it by resolving board-space effects first. The general ability to order effects cannot postpone this Leader restriction.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: restriction ‘takes effect immediately’; general freedom to order effects cannot postpone it.

answers.answer: In four players with four different positive strengths and no worms, first, second and third place each receive the corresponding printed reward; fourth receives no reward. The Conflict winner (highest strength) takes the Conflict card.
answers.evidence: Combat resolution: in four players first/second/third can receive rewards; highest strength wins and takes first reward/card; 0 strength no reward; fourth-rank reward is not provided.
